Answer: C
Reason: The CT images (Figures 4a and 4b) reveal multiple hyperdense, branching opacities within the pulmonary arteries, which are characteristic of acrylic cement emboli. This finding explains the intraoperative drop in end-tidal CO2 (due to increased dead space ventilation from vascular obstruction) and the post-operative radiographic appearance of prominent vessels in the upper and ventral lung areas caused by cement filling the vasculature.
